item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_pretrained_only","answer":"All protein examples named in the question are members of the same SCOPe family: a.4.1.9, the TALE-type DNA-binding homeodomain family within the homeodomain-like superfamily a.4.1. They therefore share not just the all-alpha homeodomain-like fold a.4 but also homologous, TALE-specific repeat-length insertions in the helix-turn-helix DNA-binding domain. The repeat-length distinction is a family-level diagnostic: TALE homeodomains such as PBC/Meis/PKNOX/TGIF/Iroquois/CUTL/HMBOX-like examples carry the three-residue insertion that lengthens the loop between helices 1 and 2, while the more distant homeodomain-like proteins outside a.4.1.9 should not be treated as equivalent templates for that TALE insertion or for TALE-family DNA-binding specificity. This supports assigning TAL effector repeat lengths only by selecting representatives inside a.4.1.9; homology, function transfer, and structural templating should be limited to that family or explicitly treated as fold/superfamily-level analogies when reaching beyond it.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}

{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q018_tal_effector_repeat_lengths","answer":"d2kq5a_, d3v6pa_, and d4cj9a_ are all assigned to SCOPe family a.298.1.1 because the classified unit is the homologous TAL-effector central repeat fold, not a fixed-length whole protein. TAL effectors contain tandem, nearly 34-residue repeats that each form a paired-helix unit; different structures can contain a short repeat fragment, many consecutive repeats, or an engineered array with a different repeat count, so their SCOPe domains can have very different chain lengths while still being the same repeat-family architecture. The evolutionary and functional transfer that is safe here is at the level of the Xanthomonas TAL-effector repeat scaffold and its repeat-variable diresidue DNA-recognition logic; the exact DNA specificity, target sequence, curvature, and array length depend on repeat number and RVD composition and should not be copied from one representative to another merely because all three domains are in a.298.1.1. In SCOPe terms, a.298 is an all-alpha TAL-effector repeat fold, a.298.1 is its TAL-effector-repeat superfamily, and a.298.1.1 is the TAL-effector family, so the shared assignment reflects homology of the repeating structural module despite expansion and contraction of the tandem array.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
